questions.question: The young woman ______ volunteered at the local health clinic was awarded a certificate of appreciation.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun 'who' is used to refer to a person functioning as the subject of the relative clause ('the young woman who volunteered').

questions.question: Many students feel fortunate to participate in community services that support underprivileged children. What is the closest contextual meaning of 'fortunate'?
questions.explanation: In the Unit 7 reading text on community service, 'fortunate' contextually means being lucky, favored, or receiving a rewarding opportunity.

questions.question: The book ______ describes the benefits of youth voluntary work is available in our school library.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun 'which' (or 'that') is used to refer to objects, things, or non-human subjects ('The book which describes...').

questions.question: Feel free to ______ at my office whenever you need guidance on your voluntary project.
questions.explanation: The phrasal verb 'drop in' means to pay a brief, informal, or casual visit to a place or person.

questions.question: What is the primary objective of engaging in community service programs?

options.text: To earn a high monthly salary from foreign donors
To help improve the community while gaining valuable life skills
To avoid attending regular school classes
To compete for political leadership roles

questions.explanation: As emphasized in Unit 7, community service aims to assist individuals and local areas without financial payment while building personal empathy and civic responsibility.

questions.question: We interviewed a doctor ______ dedicated efforts helped establish a free mobile clinic for elderly citizens.
questions.explanation: The possessive relative pronoun 'whose' is used to show ownership or relationship ('a doctor whose dedicated efforts...').

questions.question: The elderly woman ______ the student assisted every afternoon expressed her deep gratitude.
questions.explanation: 'Whom' (or 'who') is used as the object relative pronoun referring to a person receiving the action in the relative clause ('the woman whom the student assisted').

questions.question: Although balancing schoolwork and voluntary activities is demanding, students should not ______ of their academic studies.
questions.explanation: The phrasal verb 'drop out' means to withdraw, quit, or leave a school or educational program before completion.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences correctly uses commas to set off a non-defining relative clause?

options.text: Gondar which is famous for its historical castles is located in northern Ethiopia.
Gondar, which is famous for its historical castles, is located in northern Ethiopia.
Gondar, that is famous for its historical castles, is located in northern Ethiopia.
Gondar which, is famous for its historical castles is located in northern Ethiopia.

questions.explanation: Non-defining relative clauses provide extra non-essential information about a specific noun and must be enclosed in commas. Additionally, 'that' cannot replace 'which' in non-defining clauses after a comma.

questions.question: She has devoted her spare time to organizing tree-planting campaigns in her village. What is the synonym of 'devoted'?
questions.explanation: In Unit 7 reading passages, 'devoted' means giving time, effort, or loyalty enthusiastically to a worthy cause or activity.

questions.question: Hawassa is the vibrant city ______ youth groups organized an environmental sanitation project last month.
questions.explanation: The relative adverb 'where' introduces a relative clause modifying a place noun ('city where youth groups organized...').

questions.question: Analyze the two sentences: (1) 'My sister who works in Hawassa was awarded for voluntary service.' (2) 'My father, who is over 60, still participates in community development.' Which statement accurately explains their grammatical difference?

options.text: Sentence (1) contains a non-defining clause indicating the speaker has only one sister, while (2) contains a defining clause.
Sentence (1) contains a defining relative clause specifying which sister was awarded, whereas (2) contains a non-defining relative clause giving extra info about an already identified person.
Both sentences contain non-defining relative clauses that require commas around the relative pronouns.
Sentence (2) uses 'who' incorrectly because non-defining clauses must always use 'that'.

questions.explanation: Defining relative clauses (without commas) specify which individual is being discussed out of several possibilities. Non-defining clauses (with commas) add extra non-essential facts about a unique, already identified entity.

questions.question: The community center ______ the volunteers collected donations was renovated last year.
questions.explanation: In formal relative constructions involving prepositions, 'preposition + which/whom' is used ('at which' or 'in which' modifying 'community center').

questions.question: After the rain stopped, the volunteers set up tables outside and allowed the wet coats to ______ in the sun before packing them for delivery.
questions.explanation: The phrasal verb 'dry out' means to make or become completely free of moisture or water through exposure to heat or air.

questions.question: Reorder the jumbled words into a syntactically correct sentence containing a defining relative clause: 'the / whom / saw / yesterday / nurse / is / hospital / at / the / you / voluntary / .'

options.text: The nurse whom you saw at the hospital yesterday is voluntary.
You saw the nurse whom yesterday is voluntary at the hospital.
The nurse yesterday whom you saw is voluntary at the hospital.
Whom you saw the nurse at the hospital yesterday is voluntary.

questions.explanation: Standard English word order for a noun modified by a defining object relative clause is: Subject Noun ('The nurse') + Object Relative Clause ('whom you saw at the hospital yesterday') + Predicate ('is voluntary').
